clue.text: Cremation: not a bad way to communicate

indicators.note: not says a letter is left out of the shuffled word, here the single letter a
bad means the remaining letters of the word Cremation are spoiled and rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, used as written
the letter taken away, as written

explanation.surface: A grim aside that cremation is a decent enough way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'not a' drops A from CREMATION, and 'bad' shuffles the eight letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: An internal telephone or speaker system is a device for talking between rooms, so it is a means of passing messages.

clue.text: Bid type that's top — not bottom!

parts.note: taken as written
the rump is the backside or bottom

explanation.surface: An exclamation contrasting top and bottom, as if about a card bid.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge a no-trump contract outranks every suit bid at the same level, hence 'top'; the joke is that the answer read in two halves says 'not bottom'.
explanation.definitionFit: In contract bridge, a no-trump call is the highest-ranking denomination of bid at any given level.

clue.text: Sailor accompanies ancient character in spirit

indicators.note: accompanies says the sailor goes along with, here after, the old letter

parts.note: eth is a letter of the Old English alphabet
OS is ordinary seaman, a common crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor keeping company with an old-timer in good spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: The characteristic spirit or guiding beliefs of a group or era is its defining ethos-like culture.

clue.text: Sheep hearts I've taken up into bed

indicators.note: into says the turned letters are placed inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
H is the card-playing abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: Someone has carried their sweethearts up to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheviot is a hardy breed of sheep named after the hills on the English-Scottish border.

clue.text: Doctor straddling old exercise bike

indicators.note: straddling says the doctor's letters sit either side of the rest

parts.note: MD is Doctor of Medicine
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A doctor sitting astride an old exercise bike.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-powered motorcycle with pedals is a kind of motorised two-wheeler.

clue.text: Alexander imbibing hot mixed drink

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the name takes in the letter for hot

parts.note: Sandy is a familiar short form of Alexander
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A man called Alexander drinking a hot mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This British pub drink is beer combined with lemonade, so it is literally a mixed drink.

clue.text: Admires pulsating weapon

indicators.note: pulsating suggests the letters throb and move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by a throbbing weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol or other gun carried at the hip is a personal weapon worn on the body.

clue.text: Almost lost Asian ruler in Russian city

indicators.note: almost says the word for lost is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: gone astray means lost
a khan is a ruler in Central Asia

explanation.surface: An Asian ruler who has nearly lost his way in a Russian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is a port city on the Volga delta in southern Russia.

clue.text: Unsuccessful student making fresh start at Rugby

definitions.meaning: someone who abandons a course before finishing it
in rugby union, a kick from the 22-metre line to restart play

explanation.surface: A failing pupil getting a second chance at Rugby School.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby looks like the public school, which suits the student; it is the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a person who leaves education early and a drop-kick restart in rugby.

clue.text: Sorceress being non-starter in desire

indicators.note: a non-starter here has lost its first letter

parts.note: a witch is a female sorcerer

explanation.surface: A sorceress who fails to start, despite her longing.
explanation.definitionFit: A restless craving to do something is a figurative urge, as in an itch to travel.

clue.text: Voyagers make haste

definitions.meaning: a group of people travelling together on an organised journey
to act with speed; the noun also means promptness

explanation.surface: Travellers urging each other to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a travelling party of explorers and, in older usage, speed or haste.

clue.text: Cereal covers uniform in slippery slime

indicators.note: covers says the shuffled letters wrap around the uniform letter
slippery suggests the letters slide out of place

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A breakfast cereal coated in a uniform layer of slime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippery' rearranges SLIME to MESLI, and 'covers' wraps those letters round U.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss breakfast mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit is a cereal dish.

clue.text: Stop to assist returning dad and lad

indicators.note: returning says the word for help comes back the other way

parts.note: to aid is to assist
pa is a word for dad
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A plea to stop and help a returning father and boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a verb but is an organ stop.
explanation.definitionFit: On a pipe organ, a principal flue register is called by this name, so it is a kind of organ stop.

clue.text: Saw report and article after hours in AGM

indicators.note: in says the built-up letters sit inside the meeting letters

parts.note: annual general meeting, taken as written

indicators.note: after says the article comes after the letter for hours

parts.note: a pop is a bang, a report
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone saw a report and an article late at the annual general meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb but is the noun for a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying, and a pithy maxim is the same thing.

clue.text: Headless insect found in dish that's smoked

indicators.note: found in says the trimmed insect is placed inside the dish

parts.note: paella is a Spanish rice dish

indicators.note: headless says the insect loses its first letter

parts.note: a gnat is a small flying insect

explanation.surface: A headless insect turns up in a dish of smoked food.
explanation.definitionFit: A long thin cigar is something people light and puff on.

clue.text: See court painter beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded says the painter's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was principal painter to Charles II

explanation.surface: A command to look at a court painter who has been executed.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely, in Cambridgeshire, is a cathedral city with one.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's seat or diocese, and Ely is the seat of an English bishop.

clue.text: Dislike revealed in clash at Edgbaston

indicators.note: revealed in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Bad feeling shown in a confrontation at the Edgbaston cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgbaston is a Test cricket ground in Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislike someone strongly is to loathe them, so the two verbs are near-synonyms.

clue.text: French plane one ditched in river

indicators.note: ditched means dropped, so one letter is taken out of the plane

parts.note: avion is French for aeroplane
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A French aircraft that came down in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditched' looks like a plane landing on water, but it signals dropping a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avon is the name of several English rivers, including Shakespeare's.

clue.text: Minister coming north books to tour second state

indicators.note: to tour means to go round, so these letters surround the second
in a down clue, coming north means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
a mo is a moment or second

explanation.surface: A clergyman heading north with books on tour of a second state.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermont is one of the fifty United States, in New England.

clue.text: African hell — and home to Scotsman!

parts.note: the abyss is the bottomless pit of hell
in means at home
Ian is a typical Scottish name

explanation.surface: An exclamation that Africa is hell, and home to a Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia was the old name of Ethiopia, so someone from there is an Ethiopian, a native of Africa.

clue.text: Structure made with expert technique

parts.note: arch means chief or expert, as in an arch-rogue
a way of doing something is a technique

explanation.surface: A building put up using skilled methods.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage under a curved span is a piece of architecture, a built form.

clue.text: Perhaps Mister Solo's initial devotion?

indicators.note: initial picks the opening letter of the name

parts.note: a prayer is an act of devotion

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a Mister Solo is a man of prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister' looks like a title; it is a device that mists, such as a plant spray.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant mister is a device that emits a fine spray of water, an example of the answer.

clue.text: Ace companion in Belfast fire?

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace
Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, NI
a mate is a companion

explanation.surface: A top-notch friend in a Belfast blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like flames; it is the verb meaning to inspire.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone with enthusiasm is to enliven or inspire them.

clue.text: Finding fault is vital

definitions.meaning: inclined to judge harshly and censure

explanation.surface: A claim that carping is essential.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both disapproving judgement and crucial importance, as in a key moment.

clue.text: Top removed from cleaning liquid for drain

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is taken off

parts.note: bleach is a household cleaning liquid

explanation.surface: Instructions for pouring a cleaning fluid down the plughole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drain' looks like a plughole; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To percolate liquid through soil so minerals wash away is to drain them out.

clue.text: Recover for example in wet weather

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation sits inside the weather word

parts.note: rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Getting back to normal in rainy conditions, say.
explanation.definitionFit: To get back something lost is to win it back, the same as to retrieve it.

clue.text: Peer outside entrance to Lords in coat

indicators.note: outside says the looking word sits round the letter

parts.note: to peer is to gaze

indicators.note: entrance to picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A peer in his coat waiting outside the entrance to the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' suggests a lord; it is the verb to look.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy coating, as on pottery or pastry, is a thin layer applied over a surface.

clue.text: Troubled lad we care about, tired of life

indicators.note: about says the worry word goes round the shuffled letters

parts.note: care means anxiety, worry

indicators.note: troubled says the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A troubled young man whom we care about, weary of living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubled' looks like it describes the lad, but it is the anagram signal for 'lad we'; 'care' is the noun meaning anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone jaded and exhausted by existence has lost their appetite for living.

clue.text: Semite in Basra disheartened and sent back

indicators.note: sent back says the remaining letters are read in reverse
disheartened means losing the middle letter, the heart of the word

explanation.surface: A Semitic man in Basra, downcast and sent home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' drops S from BASRA, leaving BARA, and 'sent back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabs speak a Semitic language, so an Arab is one of the Semitic peoples.

clue.text: Firmly fixed in place close to boundary

parts.note: stead means place, as in 'in his stead'

indicators.note: close to means the end of, so the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something firmly planted near the boundary rope, perhaps a fielder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firmly fixed is stable and unwavering, not wobbling.

clue.text: Set start for Holmes with A Study in Scarlet

indicators.note: start for picks the first letter of the detective's name
in says the study sits inside the colour

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: A Holmes story collection set up with A Study in Scarlet, the first novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Study in Scarlet' reads as the Sherlock Holmes title, but each word works separately: the article, a room, the position word, and a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set has become firm and solid, as concrete or a jelly does.
